 Judgment

1 By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict Kamil against the judgment dated 22.05.2014 and order on sentence dated 26.05.2014 passed by  Kamil Vs. State Sh. Gaurav Rao, then Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.

sentences.text: 2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Kamil Kiryana Store, 2166, Main Bazar, Turkman Gate, Delhi- 110006.
On 05.04.2004 at about 6.15 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. Shyam Lal visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of "Dal Arhar" (ready for sale) from accused.
FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. N. R. Sharma.
The said Dal Arhar was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.

As per the report of Analyst,
sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine."

1 3
As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 25.04.2005 with the court.
Accused was summoned.

He has not exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act and get the sample analyzed by CFL.
4
Charge was framed against accused u
/ sec.2(ia) (a) (b)

1 6 ( 1 A ) o f  Kamil Vs. State PFA Act.

5 After trial, vide judgment dated 22.05.2014 accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 26.05.2014, accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 18 months and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 60 days.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined.
(ii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official.
(iii) Percentage of colour is not mentioned in PA report and thus benefit goes in favour of accused (argued orally).
7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made to join any public witnesses.

As far as this argument is concerned,
 Kamil Vs. State I have gone through the record.
In this case, it is deposed by all the PWs that they had made efforts to join independent witness before the start of the proceedings.
As no one agreed, FA Manohar Lal was joined as witness.
Moreover, this leg of argument was also done in trial court and was dealt by it from para 20 to 26 of the judgment.
I do not find any other reasoning except given by the trial court in this regard and thus that part of judgment is upheld and the submissions forwarded by Ld. counsel for appellant are rejected.
10 It is further stated that percentage of colour is not mentioned by any of the reports and thus benefit goes in favour of accused.
As far as the commodity is concerned i.e. Dal Arhar, as per Sec.29 PFA Rules, the use of colour is totally banned.
So, even if a traces of colour is found in the Dal, the same can be termed as adulterated.
So, there is no need for giving percentage of colour by the scientist i.e. PA.

R/O vs The State on 10 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148595530/
2 11
It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14 PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of jhaba etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.
Kamil Vs. State 12
As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.
However, as far as the analysis of facts are concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.
13 As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".
Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

entities.text: Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry.

entities.text:
Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in 2008 (3) RCR Kamil Vs. State (Criminal) 422 Rajinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (Punjab and Haryana), it was held by the court that when an envelop is used for weighing the sample commodity, the same must be proved as clean and free from any impurity.

entities.text: 2008 (3) RCR Kamil Vs. State (Criminal) 422 Rajinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (Punjab and Haryana)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on which surfaces the sample commodity had touched while sampling.
However, if he chooses to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.
15 In the present case, the PW1/FI Shyam Lal had stated in his cross-examination dated 27.10.2009 that the Dal was put in polythene and then it was weighed by the vendor.
However, there is no evidence as to whether this polythene was clean and free from any colour.
Thereafter, in cross-examination dated 10.06.2010 same witness stated that the Dal was weighed by putting on brown envelope.
So, this is a contradiction of a fact by Kamil Vs. State the same witness in two different statements before the same court.

So, accordingly, the prosecution failed to prove that the polythene was clean and dry and moreover,
there is contradiction to this fact as to whether it was polythene bag or envelope.
The benefit of this contradiction goes in favour of accused.

3 16
So, in these circumstances, there is violation of Rule 14 of PFA Rules and thus the benefit goes in favour of appellant.
17 So, in these circumstances, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.

18 Accused Kamil is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
19
Bail Bond u/sec.437A Cr.P.C. already furnished.
Accepted for six months.
20 TCR be sent back with copy of the order.
21 File of appeal be consigned to Record Room.
